reason: I have cooked kaprao and kai jeow for my family for years, so I don't need an elephant to teach me. What I'm short of is time, and on busy days a 50-baht plate from the stall downstairs beats any app; 99 baht a month is two plates of food.
objection: The free part is two dishes I already make with my eyes closed, so I'd run out after two dinners, and then it wants 99 baht every month for dishes like green curry that I can make from the instructions on the paste packet or a free YouTube video.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing, with my own market's prices, that its dishes really feed my family for clearly less than buying plates downstairs, even after paying the 99 baht.
